channels.name: Ship landing page
channels.description: Design, build, and ship a high-converting Astro landing page.
channels.spec:
Goal: Ship a focused marketing landing page — hero, proof, features, FAQ, and a single CTA. Not a product app.

This Space runs on OpenBot cloud (Linux, Node 24). The human is in the browser at openbot.one. They cannot open localhost on this machine.

## Stack (do not substitute)
- Astro with static output (`output: 'static'`). TypeScript. Tailwind CSS.
- pnpm. ESM (`"type": "module"`).
- Do not use Next.js, Remix, Nuxt, or a React SPA for a marketing page. Do not add auth, billing, dashboards, or an app shell — those belong in Ship paid MVP.
- Production: push to GitHub and deploy as static hosting (prefer Cloudflare Pages). Do not self-host, Dockerize, or provision a VPS.

## Cloud preview (required)
- Add `cloudflared` as a **devDependency** (do not assume a global install; this image does not ship it). Add `concurrently` or a small `scripts/dev.mjs` so one command starts the site and the tunnel.
- `pnpm dev` MUST start Astro on `127.0.0.1:4321` and run `cloudflared tunnel --url http://127.0.0.1:4321` (Cloudflare quick tunnel — no Cloudflare account).
- Parse the `https://*.trycloudflare.com` URL from cloudflared logs and print `Public preview: <url>`. Share that HTTPS URL with the human. Never tell them to visit localhost, 127.0.0.1, or a LAN IP.
- A new tunnel URL is issued on every restart — share the new one. Do not use ngrok, named Cloudflare tunnels, or a self-hosted reverse proxy.

## Page
- One page, one primary CTA above the fold (waitlist, signup interest, or buy — whatever the human asked).
- Sections: hero, social proof, feature grid, FAQ. Real copy from the brief — no lorem ipsum, no placeholder company names once the product is known.
- Semantic HTML, mobile-first, accessible (labels, contrast, keyboard). Meta title/description, Open Graph, favicon.
- Keep JS minimal (Astro islands only if a form or accordion needs it). Add a stub analytics hook (Plausible or similar) behind an env flag.
- Waitlist/email capture can be a client form with a success state. No database, no auth.

## Agents
- Claude Code implements the site, copy sections, analytics hooks, `pnpm dev` + tunnel, and deploy config.
- GitHub hosts the repository.
- Firecrawl scrapes a reference URL when the human provides one (messaging, branding, visuals). Rebuild a distinct page; do not copy verbatim.

## Done when
- `pnpm dev` is running, a public HTTPS preview URL is in the thread, and the page matches the brief on mobile and desktop.

starterPrompts.prompt: Ship an Astro landing page for a new SaaS with a waitlist CTA (hero, proof, features, FAQ, email capture). @claude-code can implement it and expose a public preview via the cloudflared tunnel on pnpm dev. @github can host the repository.

starterPrompts.prompt: I will paste a competitor or inspiration URL. @firecrawl can scrape messaging, branding, and visuals. @claude-code can rebuild a distinct Astro landing page from that research and share the public tunnel preview. @github can host the repository.

channels.name: Ship paid MVP
channels.description: Ship a paid MVP: Vite + React frontend, Express API, auth, payments, and email.
channels.spec:
Goal: Ship a paid MVP — something a person can sign up for, pay for, and get a confirmation email.

This Space runs on OpenBot cloud (Linux, Node 24). The human is in the browser at openbot.one. They cannot open localhost on this machine. Keep the first slice narrow: one persona, one paid action, one success email.

## Stack (do not substitute)
Two processes. Not a fullstack monolith.

- **Frontend:** Vite + React + TypeScript. React Router. Tailwind is fine. Call the API with relative `/api` URLs.
- **Backend:** a thin Express (or Hono) TypeScript server. JSON REST. Stripe webhooks, Resend, and any secret-bearing work live only here.
- **Do not** use Next.js, Remix, Nest, Redwood, or other fullstack frameworks. No React Server Components, no server actions.
- pnpm. ESM. Layout:

      frontend/    Vite React app (port 5173)
      backend/     Express/Hono API (port 3001)
      package.json root scripts + .env.example

- Vite `server.proxy`: `/api` → `http://127.0.0.1:3001` so the browser uses one origin.

## Cloud preview (required)
- Add `cloudflared` as a **devDependency** (do not assume a global install; this image does not ship it). Add `concurrently` or a small `scripts/dev.mjs` so one command starts frontend, backend, and the tunnel.
- `pnpm dev` MUST start both processes and run `cloudflared tunnel --url http://127.0.0.1:5173` (Cloudflare quick tunnel — no Cloudflare account). Tunnel the Vite port only; `/api` is proxied.
- Parse the `https://*.trycloudflare.com` URL from cloudflared logs and print `Public preview: <url>`. Share that HTTPS URL with the human. Never tell them to visit localhost, 127.0.0.1, or a LAN IP.
- Use that public origin for Supabase Auth redirect URLs and the Stripe webhook endpoint (`https://<tunnel>/api/stripe/webhook`). Quick tunnels change URL on restart — update those callbacks and share the new preview URL. Do not use ngrok, named Cloudflare tunnels, or a self-hosted reverse proxy.

## Product slice
- **Auth + data:** Supabase Auth and Postgres (and Storage only if the slice needs it). Verify JWTs on the server; service role key stays on the backend.
- **Payments:** Stripe Checkout (subscription, one-time, or metered — matching the brief). Create sessions on the server. Fulfill in the webhook (`checkout.session.completed` / invoice events). Never put the Stripe secret in the frontend.
- **Email:** Resend sends the success email (welcome, receipt, or magic link). Trigger from the webhook or auth flow, not from the browser.
- Ship the happy path first: sign up → pay → land on a confirmation screen → receive email. Settings, teams, admin, and extra CRUD wait.

## Secrets
- Document every variable in `.env.example`. Load them on the backend. Never commit `.env`.
- Never ask the human to paste API keys into chat. Tell them to add variables in OpenBot Settings (Stripe, Supabase, Resend). Publishable/anon keys may ship to the frontend; secret and service-role keys must not.

## Agents
- Claude Code implements the app, `pnpm dev` + tunnel, and wiring.
- GitHub hosts the repository.
- Supabase provides auth, Postgres, and storage.
- Stripe handles checkout, customers, and subscriptions or one-time payments.
- Resend sends transactional email.

## Done when
- `pnpm dev` is running, a public HTTPS preview URL is in the thread, and a reviewer can sign up, pay (Stripe test mode), and receive the confirmation email.

starterPrompts.label: Subscription SaaS
starterPrompts.prompt: Ship a subscription SaaS MVP as a Vite React frontend plus a thin Express API. @supabase can handle auth and Postgres. @stripe can take Checkout for the plan. @resend can send the welcome email. @claude-code can implement it and share the public cloudflared preview from pnpm dev. @github can host the repository.

starterPrompts.prompt: Ship a one-time purchase MVP that unlocks access after payment. Vite React frontend, Express API. @stripe can charge once. @supabase can store accounts. @resend can send the receipt. @claude-code can implement it and share the public tunnel preview. @github can host the repository.

starterPrompts.label: Usage-billed API
starterPrompts.prompt: Ship a usage-billed API MVP: Express API plus a thin Vite React dashboard. @supabase can store users and usage. @stripe can meter billing. @resend can send receipts. @claude-code can implement it and share the public cloudflared preview from pnpm dev. @github can host the repository.
